gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the two kits it showed have been tested side by side by the same lab. LinkdHOME (David Mead) found the eufy E340's daytime picture stays readable to 6.7 m against 2.3 m for the SwitchBot Smart Video Doorbell. On battery, the E340 still had 74% after 30 days, while the SwitchBot was down to 50% and died at 47 days. Expert Reviews also measured 11.5 s from an E340 button press to a live picture on the phone.
standout_why: I checked the cited Smart Home Perfected guide (2026-10-07), which says 'we did not test them hands on' and only repeats listing specs (16 ft night vision, 5000 mAh, 'about 50 days' TKMARS rating). I also checked the cited eufy E340+E10 bundle page, which gives no timings and says only 'Instant Playback, No Waiting'. The top result, WorthRated, is specs 'based on the current Amazon listing rather than independent hands-on testing' and doesn't include either kit. None of these pages has a measured alert time, live-view time, readable distance or battery drain from a named tester.
decides: This settles the choice between ChatGPT's two catalog cards. The eufy E340 + E10 ($419.99 today at eufy US, not the $399.98 ChatGPT showed) clearly wins on picture: a readable face at about 3x the distance in daylight. In LinkdHOME's battery test it also lasted longer (74% left at 30 days vs 50%, SwitchBot dead at 47 days). The SwitchBot ($149.99 with the 4.3-inch monitor in the box) costs $270 less, but LinkdHOME measured 0% package detection and 46% human-detection accuracy for it. The eufy's weak point is the phone alert, not the picture: Expert Reviews timed 6.2 s to the alert and 11.5 s to live video, against 5.1 s total for a Tapo D230S1. This matters less to a shopper who answers at the indoor screen. Recommend the eufy kit for image quality and battery, and the SwitchBot for budget buyers who mainly want a simple screen.
